scenario: AITA for telling my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together? | My girlfriend expects me to build a future for us. A little back story: She's a student right now and works part time but barely makes enough to pay her rent/school fees. I'm 24 and work a minimum wage + commission job, I have barely any money saved so she doesn't understand why I spend so much money/time with family We've been dating 3 years with no problems except for this, we love each other and live independent lives but she worries that I'm too focused on helping my family and making them happy instead of building a future for us. She's working as much as she can to pay her bills but because shes a student and also doing her required interning she can't work much more. She doesnt ever ask me for money to help her right now because she wants me to save up. She doesn't have a family like mine so she doesn't understand, my family is close and I really want to take care of them. She says that I'm supposed to be worrying about my own future right now. She says that she doesn't understand because my mom recently received about ~100k for a settlement and bought a house and a new car and I shouldn't be worrying about helping when they seem fine. She is angry that I dont take my life seriously, I've been trying to get my real estate license for a few months now but cant find the time to study because of how demanding my family is, they get really angry/sad when I'm not around for family events and I understand why, we're a close family. I get where shes coming from but I cant drop my family. I told her all of this and she got angry saying that shes not asking me to abandon my family, she just wants to make sure we have a solid foundation before we worry about helping my family. And I cant build a future if I'm always with them. She expects me to start saving up money for a downpayment on a house while she finishes and gets her degree and can start helping as well but I keep telling her my family needs me first. We had a particularly heated fight, the worst we've ever had last night and she said she feels like I'll never care enough about my future and I'm supposed to be building one for myself and her and she can't be with someone like that. She said if I really feel like helping my family comes before my own future than that is my choice but she's going to have no choice but to worry about herself from now on and plan a future where shes her only priority because I make it sound like I don't want to be part of it. Shes stopped mentioning anything about it and is now talking about saving up for a one bedroom apartment and a car for herself (she lives in a basement). She seems so sad but I cant help but feel like shes wrong for even asking me to not help my family. I dont know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family will always come first. AITA for telling her my family and their needs have to come before her and our future together?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together. Let me start by understanding the situation better. We've been dating for three years, and we've had a good relationship without major issues except for this one. She's a student working part-time, barely making enough to cover her rent and school fees. I'm 24, working a minimum wage plus commission job, and I don't have much savings. She doesn't ask me for money because she wants me to save up, but she's worried that I'm too focused on helping my family and not building a future for us. My family is really close, and I feel a strong responsibility to take care of them. Recently, my mom received a settlement of about $100k, bought a house and a new car, but I still feel the need to help them. She doesn't understand why I spend so much time and money on my family when we're trying to build our future together. She's angry that I'm not taking my life seriously, especially since I've been trying to get my real estate license but can't find the time because my family is so demanding. We had a really heated fight last night, the worst we've ever had. She feels like I'll never care enough about my future and that I'm supposed to be building one for myself and her. She said she can't be with someone who doesn't prioritize her and that if I choose to help my family over our future, she has no choice but to worry about herself and plan a future where she's her only priority. Now she's talking about saving up for her own one-bedroom apartment and a car, living in a basement. She seems really sad, but I can't help feeling like she's wrong for asking me to not help my family. I don't know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family comes first. So, is it right or wrong for me to prioritize my family over her and our future? Let me think about this step by step. First, I need to consider the importance of family versus a romantic relationship. Families are often considered a primary source of support and love, and many people feel a strong obligation to help their family members. On the other hand, a romantic partner is someone you choose to build a life with, and they often expect similar levels of commitment and prioritization. In this case, my girlfriend feels that I'm not taking our future seriously because I'm too focused on my family. She's worried about our ability to build a solid foundation together, especially since I'm not saving money for a down payment on a house or focusing on my career goals. She's even started planning her own future without me, which is a significant step. I, on the other hand, feel that my family's needs are more immediate and that I can't abandon them. I understand where she's coming from, but I can't drop my family responsibilities. I've tried to explain this to her, but she's still upset and feels like I'm not prioritizing our relationship. I need to evaluate whether it's fair to my girlfriend to always put my family first. Relationships require compromise and mutual effort. If I consistently prioritize my family over her and our future, it might lead to resentment and eventually the breakdown of our relationship. However, I also need to consider the cultural and personal values that make family so important to me. In some cultures, family comes before everything else, and that's a deeply ingrained belief. If that's the case, then it's not a matter of right or wrong, but rather a clash of values between me and my girlfriend. Another angle to consider is the practical aspects of our future together. If I'm not saving money or focusing on my career because I'm helping my family, it might hinder our ability to build a stable life together. My girlfriend is trying to finish her degree and work towards a better future, but if I'm not contributing in the way she expects, it could create financial strain and stress. I also need to think about communication. Have we had open and honest conversations about our expectations and needs? It seems like we have, but perhaps we need to find a middle ground where both our family responsibilities and our future together are addressed. Maybe we can set boundaries or find ways to balance both. In the end, it's a tough situation because both sides have valid points. My family is important to me, and I feel a responsibility to help them. However, my girlfriend is also important, and she deserves to feel that our future is a priority. It might require some compromise or reevaluating how much time and resources I'm dedicating to my family versus our relationship. I'm not sure if I'm being an asshole or not. It's possible that I'm being too rigid in my priorities, but it's also possible that my girlfriend doesn't fully understand the importance of family to me. We both need to work on understanding each other's perspectives and finding a way to move forward together.
